subject: Account throttling: reconciliation, root cause and proposed credit
messages:
From: Miguel Torres <miguel@novapay.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Cc: Aisha Khan <finance@novapay.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Spike of 429s during peak checkout window

Hi Camila —

We started seeing a surge of 429 errors between 08:45-09:10 PDT yesterday. Several checkout flows failed intermittently and our ops alerted us. I attached a small sample of request IDs and response headers.

Impact: ~2% of checkouts returned 429; we had to engage a manual retry in the client. This impacted revenue for a ~25-minute window.

Can you confirm whether this was a tenant-level throttling event on your side or something in our integration? We also need a short postmortem and any proposed restitution for the affected window.

Attached: novapay-429-samples.log (text)

Thanks,
Miguel
Miguel Torres
Head of Platform, NovaPay
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Miguel Torres <miguel@novapay.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Aisha Khan <finance@novapay.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2026 09:18:35 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike of 429s during peak checkout window

Miguel — thanks for the sample and the heads up. I'm escalating this to our infra team and will coordinate an immediate triage.

Planned steps:
- Sean to run initial ratecap / routing check and share metrics (ETA 30–45m).
- We'll confirm whether the tenant saw an applied burst-window or namespace mismatch.
- If this is on our side, we'll prepare a remediation summary and propose a credit for the impacted window.

Could you also share the SDK client version and whether retries were client-side or server-mediated? That will help isolate retry behavior.

I'll circle back with an internal summary and a customer-facing remediation note.

—Camila
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Miguel Torres <miguel@novapay.com>, Aisha Khan <finance@novapay.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2026 10:03:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike of 429s during peak checkout window

Quick technical summary (preliminary):

What we ran: looked at routing logs, tenant quota ledger, and the per-namespace window aggregator for tenant ID nova-001.
Findings:
- Between 08:46:12 and 09:09:58 PDT we observed an elevated token accounting spike that matched NovaPay's request IDs.
- Root cause: a recently-deployed quota aggregation change (rollout on 2026-06-05) introduced a corner-case where short-lived burst requests executed in a different aggregation window. The burst-window size was effectively counted twice for a subset of sequences from IPs in your region, which pushed the tenant over the enforced ratecap for ~23 minutes.
- Mitigation applied: at 09:12 we pushed a hotfix that corrected the aggregation key lookup; 429s returned to baseline within 3 minutes.

Attachments: redwood-ratecap-metrics-20260607.csv (per-minute accounting for nova-001)

Immediate next steps we took:
1) Rolled back the aggregation change for the global rollout and applied a targeted rule to avoid double-counting for your tenant. 
2) Added a temporary soft-fail path for eligible checkouts so retries would be honored client-side for 1 hour after the window.
3) We're adding a guard to the rollout pipeline to prevent the specific key-collision in future deploys.

I'll compile a one-page executive summary for you and the ops/finance teams.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Miguel Torres <miguel@novapay.com>, Aisha Khan <finance@novapay.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Jun 2026 12:07:44 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: reconciliation, remediation summary, and credit proposal

Miguel / Aisha —

Thanks again for raising this. Attached is our executive summary and the per-minute accounting (see attached CSV). Key points:

- Root cause: quota aggregation key collision following a 2026-06-05 rollout; resulted in temporary double-counting of burst tokens for a subset of NovaPay requests.
- Timeline: detection 08:46 — mitigation rolled at 09:12 — normalization by 09:15 PDT on 2026-06-07. Total affected window: ~23 minutes.
- Customer impact: ~2% of checkouts returned 429 in that window — you already logged this with ops and provided request samples (thanks).

Remediation and restitution proposal:
- We propose a one-time billing credit equivalent to 100% of API usage charges for the affected 23-minute window. Estimated credit: $1,920 (we'll confirm exact amount with finance).
- Permanent fix: patched the aggregation lookup and added pre-deploy checks to prevent key collisions; an additional guard will be added to staging tests.
- Follow-up deliverables: 1-page executive summary (attached), metrics CSV, and a deployment checklist update.

Next actions for your team:
- Please confirm acceptance of the proposed credit and your preferred contact for paperwork (Aisha indicated finance).
- If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute postmortem call next week to walk through the fix and the mitigations.

Attachments: redwood-exec-summary-20260609.pdf, redwood-ratecap-metrics-20260607.csv

Apologies for the disruption — we're committed to preventing recurrence.

Regards,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0131
From: Miguel Torres <miguel@novapay.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Cc: Aisha Khan <finance@novapay.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Jun 2026 16:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: reconciliation, remediation summary, and credit proposal

Camila / Sean —

Thank you for the clear summary and the fast remediation. We accept the proposed credit and Aisha will take the paperwork forward. Please route the final credit number and a short invoice/adjustment memo to finance@novapay.com and cc me.

We'd also like to book the 30-minute postmortem call — can you share available slots next week? Prefer mornings PST.

Appreciate the responsiveness.

—Miguel
